title: feat(ai): implement provider network safeguards (allowlist, timeouts, size limits, redirects)
problem: The provider interface and response validation are specified, but the outbound HTTP policy itself (destination allowlist, timeouts, response-size limits, redirect validation, SSRF protection, fail-closed behavior) is not implemented.
why: Without an enforced network policy, enabling a provider becomes an SSRF and data-exfiltration risk.
scope: Implement a feature-gated HTTP client that enforces an explicit destination allowlist.
Enforce connect/read timeouts, a hard response-size limit, and redirect validation.
Deny loopback, link-local, and private-range destinations; fail closed on any violation.
guidance: Centralize all policy in one module so it can be audited in isolation.
Validate allowlist entries during configuration loading and reject invalid ones.
acceptance: Disabled by default and absent from the default feature set
A clear error is returned when policy is violated
tests: Invalid URL and malformed response tests
security: Security-critical; requires focused review and adversarial tests.
dod: Merged behind a non-default feature with all safeguards tested.

title: feat(parser): extract direct intra-file function calls
problem: Rules cannot see which same-file helper a function calls, so behavior performed in helpers is invisible.
why: A direct-call map is the foundation for interprocedural analysis and reduces false positives.
scope: Build a per-function map of direct calls to functions defined in the same file, with spans.
Expose the map on the parsed source and analysis context.
guidance: Resolve callee names best-effort; record unresolved calls as unknown.
acceptance: Tests cover nested modules and collisions
security: Never fabricate edges; ambiguity is recorded, not guessed.

title: feat(parser): summarize transitive helper authorization and TTL effects
problem: Even with direct calls, rules need to know whether a helper transitively performs authorization or TTL management.
why: This is the single largest source of false positives for SS-001 and SS-006 today.
scope: Compute per-function summaries over the direct-call map using a bounded fixed-point.
Mark whether a function or its helpers call require_auth or manage TTL.
guidance: Cap recursion depth and iteration count; document the bound.
Handle recursive and mutually recursive helpers without hanging.
acceptance: Summaries correct for nested and recursive helpers
security: Bound computation to avoid pathological cost on hostile input.

title: feat(rules): use helper summaries in SS-001 and SS-006
problem: SS-001 and SS-006 still report entry points whose authorization or TTL handling happens in a helper.
why: Consuming helper summaries removes well-known false positives without weakening detection.
scope: Update SS-001 and SS-006 to consider transitive helper summaries.
Add negative fixtures where a helper authorizes or extends TTL.
guidance: Keep the change conservative: only suppress when a helper summary proves the behavior.
acceptance: Docs updated with the new behavior
security: Do not reduce true-positive detection; add negatives only where proven.

title: feat(engine): detect inline suppression directives from comments
problem: There is no way to suppress a specific finding at a specific source location, and no parser for suppression comments.
why: Targeted suppression is essential to adopt a scanner without weakening rules project-wide.
scope: Parse adjacent comments of the form `// soroban-scan: ignore SS-XXX` with an optional reason.
Match directives to the nearest applicable item or finding location.
guidance: Ignore directives that appear inside string literals or comments not adjacent to code.
Keep the pattern documented and stable.
acceptance: Directives detected and exposed with their targets
tests: Adversarial test for directives inside strings
security: Suppressions must be explicit and auditable.

title: feat(engine): apply inline suppressions and report suppressed counts
problem: Even when suppression directives are detected, the engine neither applies them nor surfaces how many findings were suppressed.
why: Suppressions must be applied consistently and remain visible so they cannot hide findings silently.
scope: Apply detected suppressions during the scan.
Count suppressed findings in statistics and expose them in terminal, JSON, and SARIF.
guidance: Never silently drop findings; always report the suppressed count and reasons.
acceptance: Suppressed findings excluded from the gate but counted
